identification.summary: BRONZE SPRING is Secureworks' Counter Threat Unit (CTU) name for a China-linked group that CTU assesses with high confidence operates on behalf of China, stealing intellectual property from defense, engineering, pharmaceutical and technology companies; the same text lists UNC302 as a synonym [S1]. CTU assesses that two Chinese nationals indicted by the US DOJ in July 2020 (Li Xiaoyu and Dong Jiazhi) are members of the group [S1]. The DOJ alleged the pair ran an intrusion campaign of more than ten years against companies in the US and about ten other countries [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: The DOJ indictment alleges the pair's campaign began in 2009 [S1]. No vendor first-observed date for the BRONZE SPRING cluster itself was verified.
identification.notes: Secureworks names for other China-linked groups that also use China Chopper (BRONZE PRESIDENT, BRONZE UNION) are separate clusters and are not merged here [S1]. Wikipedia reportedly links the Guangdong State Security Department to BRONZE SPRING/UNC302, which was not verified.

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China. The DOJ alleged Li and Dong worked with, and operated with the acquiescence of, the Ministry of State Security (MSS), including officers of the Guangdong State Security Department (GSSD); some activity was for personal profit and some for the MSS [S2][S3].
attribution.confidence: Secureworks CTU assesses with high confidence that BRONZE SPRING operates on behalf of China [S1]. The DOJ alleged MSS links in an indictment; allegations are not proof of guilt, and the MSS officers were not charged [S2][S4]. Linking the indicted individuals to BRONZE SPRING is a CTU assessment, not a DOJ statement [S1].
attribution.basis: Secureworks CTU assessment (as reproduced by a Malpedia mirror) [S1]; DOJ indictment and press release, and press coverage of both [S2][S3][S4].

objectives: Theft of intellectual property and trade secrets from defense, engineering, pharmaceutical and technology companies [S1]. The DOJ alleged data was passed to the MSS or sold for financial gain [S1], and that the pair also targeted dissidents, clergy and democratic and human rights activists, including in Hong Kong and China [S2][S3].

sectors: Companies developing COVID-19 vaccines, testing technology and treatments (per indictment)
Dissidents, clergy and human rights activists
regions: United States and about ten other countries (per indictment) [S2][S3]
targeting.notes: Sector list from CTU [S1]; COVID-19 research and activist targeting from the DOJ allegations as reported [S2][S3][S4]. Press noted no immediate indication that the hackers obtained COVID-19 research [S6].

capabilities.summary: CTU describes scan-and-exploit for initial access, the China Chopper web shell for remote execution and persistence, and RAR archives given a '.jpg' extension for exfiltration [S1]. The DOJ described exploitation of known vulnerabilities in popular web server software, web application development suites and software collaboration programs, followed by web shells such as China Chopper and credential-stealing software [S3][S2].

campaigns.name: Alleged long-running global intrusion campaign
campaigns.summary: The DOJ alleged Li Xiaoyu and Dong Jiazhi compromised networks of hundreds of organizations and individuals in the US and abroad from 2009, exfiltrating trade secrets, with data passed to the MSS or sold [S1][S2][S3].

campaigns.name: DOJ indictment of Li Xiaoyu and Dong Jiazhi
campaigns.summary: An 11-count indictment from a Spokane, Washington grand jury was filed 7 July and unsealed about 21 July 2020, alleging theft from defense contractors and COVID-19 researchers and targeting of activists; the FBI issued a TLP White flash on 2020-07-21 [S2][S6][S7].

diamond.adversary: Two indicted Chinese nationals, Li Xiaoyu and Dong Jiazhi, working with MSS/GSSD officers per DOJ allegation; CTU assesses them as BRONZE SPRING members [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Scan-and-exploit of known web and collaboration software flaws, China Chopper web shells, credential stealers, RAR exfiltration disguised as .jpg [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Internet-facing victim servers used as footholds via web shells [S1][S3]. Actor-controlled infrastructure details were not verified.
diamond.victim: Defense, engineering, pharmaceutical, technology firms, COVID-19 researchers, and activists [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Mixed state-directed and personally profitable activity within the PRC contractor ecosystem; MSS received or tasked data [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Exposure of unpatched internet-facing web servers, web application suites and collaboration software [S3].

gaps: Secureworks' original BRONZE SPRING report was not opened; CTU statements come from a Malpedia mirror seen in search results (page fetch failed) [S1].

DOJ press releases and indictment (justice.gov) and the Intrusion Truth post could not be fetched; they were relied on via search-result summaries and press coverage, so details are unverified against the primary text.
The MITRE group ID is blank in the record; no MITRE group mapping or Microsoft name was verified.
Whether UNC302 (Mandiant) fully matches BRONZE SPRING scope is not verified; no Mandiant source was found.
Activity after 2020 is not documented in the sources gathered; current status of the indictment (arrest or extradition) was not found.
Dates for the CyberScoop and BleepingComputer articles are approximate (month only).
Specific CVEs and malware families other than China Chopper were not verified.
An Intrusion Truth post about the actor was dropped during fact-checking because its URL and contents could not be confirmed in search results.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing web servers and collaboration software at defense contractors, engineering and technology firms (DIB) are key terrain [S1][S3]. STEP 2: The actor rewards rapid exploitation of known vulnerabilities, so patch latency is the main defender weakness [S3]. STEP 3: Template is scan-and-exploit, then China Chopper web shell, credential theft, then RAR archives named .jpg for exfiltration [S1][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued IP theft against defense, pharma and technology targets. MDCOA is shifting to crisis-driven collection (as with COVID-19 research in 2020) against DoD-adjacent research and contractors [S2][S3]. Candidate indicators: new ASPX/web shell files on public servers, credential-dumping tools on web hosts, and large .jpg-named files that are actually RAR archives leaving the network [S1][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vulnerability disclosures for web and collaboration software and exposed contractor servers. (2) Authorities: coordinate DIB-contractor incident response through established DC3/DIB CS channels rather than direct action. (3) Mission assurance: harden and monitor internet-facing servers holding program data; hunt web shells. (4) Coordination: share indicators with FBI and civil partners given the DOJ case; note that the indicted-individual link to BRONZE SPRING is a vendor assessment [S1][S2].

provenance.importedSummary: BRONZE SPRING is a threat group that CTU researchers assess with high confidence operates on behalf of China in the theft of intellectual property from defense, engineering, pharmaceutical and technology companies. The threat group typically uses scan-and-exploit for initial access, deploys the China Chopper webshell for remote execution and persistence, and creates RAR archives with a '.jpg' file extension for data exfiltration. In July 2020 the U.S. Department of Justice indicted two Chinese hackers CTU researchers assess are members of the BRONZE SPRING threat group. The Department of Justice allege these hackers were responsible for compromising networks of hundreds of organisations and individuals in the U.S. and abroad since 2009, and that exfiltrated data would be passed to the Chinese Ministry of State Security or sold for financial gain.
